The Fubini–Study metric for a pure-state family $\psi=\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}\,e^{iS/x}$ is the real part of the quantum geometric tensor,
$$g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}=\operatorname{Re}\!\left[\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle-\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle\right].$$

Writing the logarithmic derivative in terms of the Madelung–Bohm velocities,
$$\partial_\mu\ln\psi=\frac{1}{2}\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P}+\frac{i}{x}\partial_\mu S
=\frac{m}{x}\,(u_\mu+i\pi_\mu),$$
one finds that the quantum geometric tensor equals $(m/x)^2$ times the complex covariance of the combination $u_\mu+i\pi_\mu$. Taking the real part kills the cross–terms between $u$ and $\pi$, leaving exactly the sum of their covariances:

$$g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}=\frac{m^{2}}{x^{2}}\Bigl[\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)+\operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)\Bigr]_{\mathcal{P}}.$$

Hence the proportionality factor is

$$\boxed{\dfrac{m^{2}}{x^{2}}}.$$
